facts.text: Meire Grove was founded around 1858 and became an incorporated village on December 24, 1896, with a post office operating from 1873 to 1905.
The town’s name originated from a misspelling in the 1850s, swapping the ‘y’ for an ‘i’ and adding a ‘re’ that was common in that era.
Meire Grove never received a railroad because residents opposed it, a decision that, according to locals, could have added roughly 200 more residents.
The Meire Grove Band, founded in 1883, is Minnesota’s oldest continuously operating town band, performing several concerts and parades each year.
John the Baptist Catholic Church, established in the 1800s, remains a landmark of Meire Grove’s early religious community.
